chunks: Aban, from Abu Al Jaroud, who said:

Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: 'A man cannot buy back what he has given in charity, and if he has given a house in charity to a relative, then if he wishes, he can dwell with them, and if he has given a servant in charity to a relative, she serves him, God willing.'
ai.seo_question: Can a person buy back property they have given as charity to their relatives?
ai.summary: Imam Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) establishes that while a donor generally cannot repurchase their own charity (sadaqah), exceptions exist for gifts given to relatives, allowing the donor to retain usufruct rights such as residing in the donated house or utilizing the donated servant. This ruling highlights the flexibility in Shia jurisprudence regarding family-based endowments, balancing the finality of charity with practical familial care and social cohesion.
